comments.title: Mutable default argument
comments.explanation: Using a mutable object (list) as a default argument in a function definition is a common Python pitfall. The default value is evaluated only once at function definition time, meaning all calls to f() will share the same list instance. If the list is modified, those changes persist across subsequent calls.

suggestion.explanation: Using None as a sentinel value and initializing the list inside the function body ensures that a new list is created every time the function is called without an argument, avoiding unintended side effects.

summary: The code contains a classic Python anti-pattern where a mutable object (a list) is used as a default argument. This can lead to unexpected state persistence between function calls. I have recommended using None as a default value and initializing the list inside the function.

comments.title: Resource Leak
comments.explanation: The database connection is opened but never closed, which can lead to connection pool exhaustion.

suggestion.original_code:
conn = connect_db()
    cursor = conn.cursor()

    cursor.execute("""
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users(
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
        username TEXT,
        password TEXT,
        age INTEGER
    )
    """)

    conn.commit()
suggestion.replacement_code:
with connect_db() as conn:
        cursor = conn.cursor()
        cursor.execute("""
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users(
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            username TEXT,
            password TEXT,
            age INTEGER
        )
        """)
        conn.commit()
suggestion.explanation: Using a context manager ensures the connection is closed automatically.
